provide your correct TIN. </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Caution:</B> If you don&#8217;t return Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> to the requester with
a TIN, you might be subject to backup withholding. See <I>What is backup withholding</I>, later. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>By signing the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">filled-out</FONT> form</B>, you: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">1. Certify that the TIN you are giving is correct (or you are waiting for a
number to be issued); </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">2. Certify that you are not subject to backup withholding; or </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">3. Claim exemption from backup withholding if you are a U.S. exempt payee; and </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">4. Certify to your <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> status for purposes of withholding under chapter 3 or 4 of the Code (if
applicable); and </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">5. Certify that FATCA code(s) entered on this form (if any) indicating that you are exempt from the FATCA reporting is
correct. See <I>What Is FATCA Reporting</I>, later, for further information. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note:</B> If you are a U.S. person and a requester gives you a form other
than Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> to request your TIN, you must use the requester&#8217;s form if it is substantially similar to this Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Definition of a U.S. person.</B> For federal tax purposes, you are considered a U.S. person if you are: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">An individual who is a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident alien; </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">A partnership, corporation, company, or association created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States; </TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">An estate (other than a foreign estate); or </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">A domestic trust (as defined in Regulations section <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">301.7701-7).</FONT> </TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Establishing U.S. status for purposes of chapter 3 and chapter 4 withholding.</B> Payments made to foreign persons, including certain distributions,
allocations of income, or transfers of sales proceeds, may be subject to withholding under chapter 3 or chapter 4 of the Code (sections 1441-1474). Under those rules, if a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> or other certification of <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> status has not been received, a withholding agent, transferee, or partnership (payor) generally applies presumption rules that may require the payor to withhold applicable tax from the recipient, owner,
transferor, or partner (payee). See Pub. 515, Withholding of Tax on Nonresident Aliens and Foreign Entities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following persons must
provide Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> to the payor for purposes of establishing its <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> status. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">In the case of a disregarded entity with a U.S. owner, the U.S. owner of the disregarded entity and not the disregarded entity. </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">In the case of a grantor trust with a U.S. grantor or other U.S. owner, generally, the U.S. grantor or other U.S. owner of the grantor trust and not the grantor trust. </TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">In the case of a U.S. trust (other than a grantor trust), the U.S. trust and not the beneficiaries of the trust. </TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See Pub. 515 for more information on providing a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> or a certification of
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> status to avoid withholding. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Foreign person.</B> If you are a foreign person or the U.S. branch of
a foreign bank that has elected to be treated as a U.S. person (under Regulations section <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">1.1441-1(b)(2)(iv)</FONT> or other applicable section for chapter 3 or 4 purposes), do not use Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> Instead, use the appropriate Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-8</FONT> or Form 8233 (see Pub. 515). If you are a qualified foreign pension fund under Regulations section
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">1.897(l)-1(d),</FONT> or a partnership that is wholly owned by
</P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-left:3%; width:49%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
qualified foreign pension funds, that is treated as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> person for purposes of section 1445 withholding, do not use Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> Instead, use Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-8EXP</FONT> (or other certification of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-foreign</FONT> status). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Nonresident alien who becomes a resident alien.</B> Generally, only a nonresident alien individual may use the terms of a tax treaty to reduce or eliminate
U.S. tax on certain types of income. However, most tax treaties contain a provision known as a saving clause. Exceptions specified in the saving clause may permit an exemption from tax to continue for certain types of income even after the payee has
otherwise become a U.S. resident alien for tax purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are a U.S. resident alien who is relying on an exception contained in the
saving clause of a tax treaty to claim an exemption from U.S. tax on certain types of income, you must attach a statement to Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> that specifies the following five items. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">1. The treaty country. Generally, this must be the same treaty under which you claimed exemption from tax as a nonresident alien. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">2. The treaty article addressing the income. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">3. The article number (or location) in the tax treaty that contains the saving clause and its exceptions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">4. The type and amount of income that qualifies for the exemption from tax. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">5. Sufficient facts to justify the exemption from tax under the terms of the treaty article. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Example.</I></B> Article 20 of the U.S.-China income tax treaty allows an exemption from tax for scholarship income received by a
Chinese student temporarily present in the United States. Under U.S. law, this student will become a resident alien for tax purposes if their stay in the United States exceeds 5 calendar years. However, paragraph 2 of the first Protocol to the
U.S.-China treaty (dated April&nbsp;30, 1984) allows the provisions of Article 20 to continue to apply even after the Chinese student becomes a resident alien of the United States. A Chinese student who qualifies for this exception (under paragraph
2 of the first Protocol) and is relying on this exception to claim an exemption from tax on their scholarship or fellowship income would attach to Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> a statement that includes the information described
above to support that exemption. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are a nonresident alien or a foreign entity, give the requester the appropriate completed Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-8</FONT> or Form 8233. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Backup Withholding </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>What is backup withholding?</B> Persons making certain payments to you must under certain conditions withhold and pay to the IRS 24% of such payments. This
is called &#8220;backup withholding.&#8221; Payments that may be subject to backup withholding include, but are not limited to, interest, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> interest, dividends, broker and barter exchange
transactions, rents, royalties, nonemployee pay, payments made in settlement of payment card and third-party network transactions, and certain payments from fishing boat operators. Real estate transactions are not subject to backup withholding. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">You will not be subject to backup withholding on payments you receive if you give the requester your correct TIN, make the proper
certifications, and report all your taxable interest and dividends on your tax return. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Payments you receive will be subject to backup withholding if:
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:3%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">1. You do not furnish your TIN to the requester; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:3%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">2. You do not certify your TIN when required (see the instructions for Part II for details); </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:3%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">3. The IRS tells the requester that you furnished an incorrect TIN; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:3%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">4. The IRS tells you that you are subject to backup withholding because you did not report all your interest and dividends on your tax return
(for reportable interest and dividends only); or </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:3%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">5. You do not certify to the requester that you are not subject to backup withholding,
as described in item 4 under &#8220;<I>By signing the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">filled-out</FONT> form</I>&#8221; above (for reportable interest and dividend accounts opened after 1983 only). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Certain payees and payments are exempt from backup withholding. See <I>Exempt payee code</I>, later, and the separate Instructions for the
Requester of Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> for more information. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I></I>See also<I> Establishing U.S. status for
purposes of chapter 3 and chapter 4 withholding, </I>earlier.<I> </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>What Is FATCA Reporting? </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) requires a participating foreign financial institution to report all U.S. account holders that are specified
U.S. persons. Certain payees are exempt from FATCA reporting. See <I>Exemption from FATCA reporting code</I>, later, and the Instructions for the Requester of Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> for more information. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Updating Your Information </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">You must provide updated
information to any person to whom you claimed to be an exempt payee if you are no longer an exempt payee and anticipate receiving reportable payments in the future from this person. For example, you may need to provide updated information if you are
a C corporation that elects to be an S corporation, or if you are no longer tax exempt. In addition, you must furnish a new Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> if the name or TIN changes for the account, for example, if the grantor of a
grantor trust dies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Penalties </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Failure to furnish
TIN.</B> If you fail to furnish your correct TIN to a requester, you are subject to a penalty of $50 for each such failure unless your failure is due to reasonable cause and not to willful neglect.
</P></div><div style="clear:both; height:0pt; font-size:0pt">&nbsp;</div>

</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:7pt" ALIGN="center">

<TR>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="49%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-size:7pt">Form W-9 (Rev. 3-2024)</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right"><FONT STYLE="font-size:7pt">Page</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right"><B>3</B></TD></TR></TABLE> <DIV STYLE="line-height:3.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; width:48%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Civil penalty for false information with respect to withholding.</B> If you make a false statement with no
reasonable basis that results in no backup withholding, you are subject to a $500 penalty. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Criminal penalty for falsifying information.</B> Willfully
falsifying certifications or affirmations may subject you to criminal penalties including fines and/or imprisonment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Misuse of TINs.</B> If the
requester discloses or uses TINs in violation of federal law, the requester may be subject to civil and criminal penalties. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Specific Instructions
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 1 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">You must enter one of the following on
this line; <B>do not</B> leave this line blank. The name should match the name on your tax return. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If this Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> is for a joint account (other than an account maintained by a foreign financial institution (FFI)), list first, and then circle, the name of the person or entity whose number you entered in Part I of Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> If you are providing Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> to an FFI to document a joint account, each holder of the account that is a U.S. person must provide a Form
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;<B>Individual.</B> Generally, enter the name shown on your tax return. If you have
changed your last name without informing the Social Security Administration (SSA) of the name change, enter your first name, the last name as shown on your social security card, and your new last name. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note for ITIN applicant:</B> Enter your individual name as it was entered on your <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Form&nbsp;W-7</FONT> application, line
1a. This should also be the same as the name you entered on the Form&nbsp;1040 you filed with your application. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;<B>Sole
proprietor.</B> Enter your individual name as shown on your Form 1040 on line 1. Enter your business, trade, or &#8220;doing business as&#8221; (DBA) name on line 2. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;<B>Partnership, C corporation, S corporation, or LLC, other than a disregarded entity.</B> Enter the entity&#8217;s name as shown on the
entity&#8217;s tax return on line 1 and any business, trade, or DBA name on line 2. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;<B>Other entities.</B> Enter your name as shown
on required U.S. federal tax documents on line 1. This name should match the name shown on the charter or other legal document creating the entity. Enter any business, trade, or DBA name on line 2. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;<B>Disregarded entity.</B> In general, a business entity that has a single owner, including an LLC, and is not a corporation, is
disregarded as an entity separate from its owner (a disregarded entity). See Regulations section <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">301.7701-2(c)(2).</FONT> A disregarded entity should check the appropriate box for the tax classification of its owner.
Enter the owner&#8217;s name on line 1. The name of the owner entered on line 1 should never be a disregarded entity. The name on line 1 should be the name shown on the income tax return on which the income should be reported. For example, if a
foreign LLC that is treated as a disregarded entity for U.S. federal tax purposes has a single owner that is a U.S. person, the U.S. owner&#8217;s name is required to be provided on line 1. If the direct owner of the entity is also a disregarded
entity, enter the first owner that is not disregarded for federal tax purposes. Enter the disregarded entity&#8217;s name on line 2. If the owner of the disregarded entity is a foreign person, the owner must complete an appropriate Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-8</FONT> instead of a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> This is the case even if the foreign person has a U.S. TIN. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 2 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you have a business name, trade name, DBA name,
or disregarded entity name, enter it on line 2. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 3a </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Check the appropriate box on line 3a for the U.S. federal tax classification of the person whose name is entered on line 1. Check only one box on line 3a.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8pt;"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149; Individual or</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:2pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149; Sole proprietorship</P></TD>

<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8pt;"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149; LLC classified as a partnership for U.S.
federal tax purposes or</P> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149; LLC that has filed Form 8832 or 2553 electing to be
taxed as a corporation</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-right:2pt;"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Limited liability company and enter the
appropriate tax classification:</P> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">P = Partnership,</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">C = C corporation, or</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">S = S corporation.</P></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">

<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8pt;">&#149; Partnership</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-right:2pt;">Partnership.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="4" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8pt;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="2" STYLE="BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #000000;">&nbsp;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8pt;">&#149; Trust/estate</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #000000; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #000000; padding-right:2pt;">Trust/estate.</TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 3b </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Check this box if
you are a partnership (including an LLC classified as a partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes), trust, or estate that has any foreign partners, owners, or beneficiaries, and you are providing this form to a partnership, trust, or estate, in
which you have an ownership interest. You must check the box on line 3b if you receive a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-8</FONT> (or documentary evidence) from any partner, owner, or beneficiary establishing foreign status or if you receive
a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> from any partner, owner, or beneficiary that has checked the box on line 3b. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note:</B> A
partnership that provides a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> and checks box 3b may be required to complete Schedules <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">K-2</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">K-3</FONT> (Form 1065). For more
information, see the Partnership Instructions for Schedules <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">K-2</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">K-3</FONT> (Form 1065).
</P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-left:3%; width:49%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are required to complete line 3b but fail to do so, you may not receive the information
necessary to file a correct information return with the IRS or furnish a correct payee statement to your partners or beneficiaries. See, for example, sections 6698, 6722, and 6724 for penalties that may apply. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 4 Exemptions </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are exempt from backup
withholding and/or FATCA reporting, enter in the appropriate space on line 4 any code(s) that may apply to you. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Exempt payee code. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;Generally, individuals (including sole proprietors) are not exempt from backup withholding. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;Except as provided below, corporations are exempt from backup withholding for certain payments, including interest and dividends. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;Corporations are not exempt from backup withholding for payments made in settlement of payment card or third-party network transactions.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;&#8196;&#8196;Corporations are not exempt from backup withholding with respect to attorneys&#8217; fees or gross proceeds paid to attorneys, and
corporations that provide medical or health care services are not exempt with respect to payments reportable on Form 1099-MISC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The
following codes identify payees that are exempt from backup withholding. Enter the appropriate code in the space on line 4. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">1 &#8212; An
organization exempt from tax under section 501(a), any IRA, or a custodial account under section 403(b)(7) if the account satisfies the requirements of section&nbsp;401(f)(2). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">2 &#8212; The United States or any of its agencies or instrumentalities. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">3 &#8212; A state, the District of Columbia, a U.S. commonwealth or territory, or any of their political subdivisions or instrumentalities.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">4 &#8212; A foreign government or any of its political subdivisions, agencies, or instrumentalities. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">5 &#8212; A corporation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">6
&#8212; A dealer in securities or commodities required to register in the United States, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. commonwealth or territory. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">7 &#8212; A futures commission merchant registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">8 &#8212; A real estate investment trust. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">9 &#8212; An entity registered at all times during the tax year under the Investment Company Act of 1940. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">10 &#8212; A common trust fund operated by a bank under section 584(a). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">11 &#8212; A financial institution as defined under section 581. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">12 &#8212; A middleman known in the investment community as a nominee or custodian. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">13 &#8212; A trust exempt from tax under section 664 or described in section 4947. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following chart shows types of payments that may be exempt from backup withholding. The chart applies to the exempt payees listed above, 1
through 13. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

services paid by a federal executive agency. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Exemption from FATCA reporting code.</B> The following codes identify payees that are
exempt from reporting under FATCA. These codes apply to persons submitting this form for accounts maintained outside of the United States by certain foreign financial institutions. Therefore, if you are only submitting this form for an account you
hold in the United States, you may leave this field blank. Consult with the person requesting this form if you are uncertain if the financial institution is subject to these requirements. A requester may indicate that a code is not required by
providing you with a Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> with &#8220;Not Applicable&#8221; (or any similar indication) entered on the line for a FATCA exemption code. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A &#8212; An organization exempt from tax under section 501(a) or any individual retirement plan as defined in section 7701(a)(37). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">B &#8212; The United States or any of its agencies or instrumentalities.

<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right"><B>4</B></TD></TR></TABLE> <DIV STYLE="line-height:3.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; width:48%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">C &#8212; A state, the District of Columbia, a U.S. commonwealth or territory, or any of their
political subdivisions or instrumentalities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">D &#8212; A corporation the stock of which is regularly traded on one or more established
securities markets, as described in Regulations section <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">1.1472-1(c)(1)(i).</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">E &#8212; A
corporation that is a member of the same expanded affiliated group as a corporation described in Regulations section <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">1.1472-1(c)(1)(i).</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">F &#8212; A dealer in securities, commodities, or derivative financial instruments (including notional principal contracts, futures, forwards,
and options) that is registered as such under the laws of the United States or any state. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">G &#8212; A real estate investment trust. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">H &#8212; A regulated investment company as defined in section 851 or an entity registered at all times during the tax year under the
Investment Company Act of 1940. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">I &#8212; A common trust fund as defined in section 584(a). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">J &#8212; A bank as defined in section 581. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">K &#8212; A broker. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">L &#8212;
A trust exempt from tax under section 664 or described in section 4947(a)(1). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">M &#8212; A
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> trust under a section 403(b) plan or section 457(g) plan. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note:</B> You may wish to consult with
the financial institution requesting this form to determine whether the FATCA code and/or exempt payee code should be completed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 5 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Enter your address (number, street, and apartment or suite number). This is where the requester of this Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> will
mail your information returns. If this address differs from the one the requester already has on file, enter &#8220;NEW&#8221; at the top. If a new address is provided, there is still a chance the old address will be used until the payor changes
your address in their records. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Line 6 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Enter your
city, state, and ZIP code. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Part I. Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Enter your TIN in the appropriate box.</B> If you are a resident alien and you do not have, and are not eligible to get, an SSN, your TIN is your IRS ITIN.
Enter it in the entry space for the Social security number. If you do not have an ITIN, see <I>How to get a TIN</I> below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are a
sole proprietor and you have an EIN, you may enter either your SSN or EIN. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are a single-member LLC that is disregarded as an
entity separate from its owner, enter the owner&#8217;s SSN, (or EIN, if the owner has one). If the LLC is classified as a corporation or partnership, enter the entity&#8217;s EIN. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note:</B> See <I>What Name and Number To Give the Requester</I>, later, for further clarification of name and TIN combinations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>How to get a TIN.</B> If you do not have a TIN, apply for one immediately. To apply for an SSN, get Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">SS-5,</FONT>
Application for a Social Security Card, from your local SSA office or get this form online at <I>www.SSA.gov</I>. You may also get this form by calling <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">800-772-1213.</FONT></FONT> Use
Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-7,</FONT> Application for IRS Individual Taxpayer Identification Number, to apply for an ITIN, or Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">SS-4,</FONT> Application for Employer Identification Number, to apply for
an EIN. You can apply for an EIN online by accessing the IRS website at <I>www.irs.gov/EIN</I>. Go to <I>www.irs.gov/Forms</I> to view, download, or print Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-7</FONT> and/or Form
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">SS-4.</FONT> Or, you can go to <I>www.irs.gov/OrderForms</I> to place an order and have Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-7</FONT> and/or Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">SS-4</FONT> mailed to you within
15 business days. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are asked to complete Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9</FONT> but do not have a TIN, apply for a TIN
and enter &#8220;Applied For&#8221; in the space for the TIN, sign and date the form, and give it to the requester. For interest and dividend payments, and certain payments made with respect to readily tradable instruments, you will generally have
60 days to get a TIN and give it to the requester before you are subject to backup withholding on payments. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">60-day</FONT> rule does not apply to other types of payments. You will be subject to backup withholding
on all such payments until you provide your TIN to the requester. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note:</B> Entering &#8220;Applied For&#8221; means that you have already applied for
a TIN or that you intend to apply for one soon. See also <I>Establishing U.S. status for purposes of chapter 3 and chapter 4 withholding</I>, earlier, for when you may instead be subject to withholding under chapter 3 or 4 of the Code. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Caution:</B> A disregarded U.S. entity that has a foreign owner must use the appropriate <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Form&nbsp;W-8.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Part II. Certification </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To establish to the withholding
agent that you are a U.S. person, or resident alien, sign Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-9.</FONT> You may be requested to sign by the withholding agent even if item 1, 4, or 5 below indicates otherwise. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For a joint account, only the person whose TIN is shown in Part I should sign (when required). In the case of a disregarded entity, the person
identified on line 1 must sign. Exempt payees, see <I>Exempt payee</I> code, earlier. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Signature requirements.</B> Complete the certification as
indicated in items 1 through 5 below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>1. Interest, dividend, and barter exchange accounts opened before 1984 and broker accounts
considered active during 1983.</B> You must give your correct TIN, but you do not have to sign the certification. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>2. Interest,
dividend, broker, and barter exchange accounts opened after 1983 and broker accounts considered inactive during 1983.</B> You must sign the certification or backup withholding will apply. If you are subject to backup withholding and you are merely
providing your correct TIN to the requester, you must cross out item 2 in the certification before signing the form.
</P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-left:3%; width:49%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>3. Real estate transactions.</B> You must sign the certification. You may cross out item 2
of the certification. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>4. Other payments.</B> You must give your correct TIN, but you do not have to sign the certification unless you
have been notified that you have previously given an incorrect TIN. &#8220;Other payments&#8221; include payments made in the course of the requester&#8217;s trade or business for rents, royalties, goods (other than bills for merchandise), medical
and health care services (including payments to corporations), payments to a nonemployee for services, payments made in settlement of payment card and third-party network transactions, payments to certain fishing boat crew members and fishermen, and
gross proceeds paid to attorneys (including payments to corporations). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>5. Mortgage interest paid by you, acquisition or abandonment of
secured property, cancellation of debt, qualified tuition program payments (under section 529), ABLE accounts (under section 529A), IRA, Coverdell ESA, Archer MSA or HSA contributions or distributions, and pension distributions.</B> You must give
your correct TIN, but you do not have to sign the certification. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>What Name and Number To Give the Requester </B></P>

<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:7pt" ALIGN="center">

<TR>

<TD WIDTH="48%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="49%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-size:7pt">Form W-9 (Rev. 3-2024)</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right"><FONT STYLE="font-size:7pt">Page</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right"><B>5</B></TD></TR></TABLE> <DIV STYLE="line-height:3.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; width:48%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Secure Your Tax Records From Identity Theft </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Identity theft occurs when someone uses your personal information, such as your name, SSN, or other identifying information, without your permission to commit
fraud or other crimes. An identity thief may use your SSN to get a job or may file a tax return using your SSN to receive a refund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To
reduce your risk: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">Protect your SSN, </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">Ensure your employer is protecting your SSN, and </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:6.5pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="7" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top">Be careful when choosing a tax return preparer. </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If your tax records are affected by identity
theft and you receive a notice from the IRS, respond right away to the name and phone number printed on the IRS notice or letter. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If your
tax records are not currently affected by identity theft but you think you are at risk due to a lost or stolen purse or wallet, questionable credit card activity, or a questionable credit report, contact the IRS Identity Theft Hotline at <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">800-908-4490</FONT></FONT> or submit Form 14039. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For more information, see
Pub. 5027, Identity Theft Information for Taxpayers. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Victims of identity theft who are experiencing economic harm or a systemic problem,
or are seeking help in resolving tax problems that have not been resolved through normal channels, may be eligible for Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) assistance. You can reach TAS by calling the TAS toll-free case intake line at <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">877-777-4778</FONT></FONT> or TTY/TDD <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">800-829-4059.</FONT></FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Protect yourself from suspicious emails or phishing schemes.</B> Phishing is the creation and use of email and websites designed to mimic legitimate
business emails and websites. The most common act is sending an email to a user falsely claiming to be an established legitimate enterprise in an attempt to scam the user into surrendering private information that will be used for identity theft.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The IRS does not initiate contacts with taxpayers via emails. Also, the IRS does not request personal detailed information through email
or ask taxpayers for the PIN numbers, passwords, or similar secret access information for their credit card, bank, or other financial accounts.
</P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-left:3%; width:49%;padding-right:0%;padding-bottom:8pt;overflow:visible;padding-top:3pt">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you receive an unsolicited email claiming to be from the IRS, forward this message to
<I>phishing@irs.gov</I>. You may also report misuse of the IRS name, logo, or other IRS property to the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) at
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">800-366-4484.</FONT></FONT> You can forward suspicious emails to the Federal Trade Commission at <I>spam@uce.gov</I> or report them at <I>www.ftc.gov/complaint</I>. You can contact
the FTC at <I>www.ftc.gov/idtheft</I> or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">877-IDTHEFT</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(877-438-4338).</FONT></FONT> If you have been the victim of identity theft, see
<I>www.IdentityTheft.gov</I> and Pub. 5027. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:1%; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Go to <I>www.irs.gov/IdentityTheft</I> to learn more about identity theft and how to reduce
your risk. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Privacy Act Notice </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:6.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Section&nbsp;6109 of
the Internal Revenue Code requires you to provide your correct TIN to persons (including federal agencies) who are required to file information returns with the IRS to report interest, dividends, or certain other income paid to you; mortgage
interest you paid; the acquisition or abandonment of secured property; the cancellation of debt; or contributions you made to an IRA, Archer MSA, or HSA. The person collecting this form uses the information on the form to file information returns
with the IRS, reporting the above information. Routine uses of this information include giving it to the Department of Justice for civil and criminal litigation and to cities, states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. commonwealths and territories
for use in administering their laws. The information may also be disclosed to other countries under a treaty, to federal and state agencies to enforce civil and criminal laws, or to federal law enforcement and intelligence agencies to combat
terrorism. You must provide your TIN whether or not you are required to file a tax return. Under section 3406, payors must generally withhold a percentage of taxable interest, dividends, and certain other payments to a payee who does not give a TIN
to the payor. Certain penalties may also apply for providing false or fraudulent information. </P></div><div style="clear:both; height:0pt; font-size:0pt">&nbsp;</div>

</DIV></Center>
